sections.heading: Fixed
items: On Windows, TrackCut no longer fails to start with "VCRUNTIME140_1.dll was not found" on PCs without the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable. Nothing extra needs to be installed any more.

sections.heading: Added
items: Use TrackCut from Claude. The new **MCP** button at the top of the file list shows what to paste into Claude Desktop, or the one line to run for Claude Code, already pointing at where TrackCut is installed. Claude can then list a folder's recordings, find a recording's tracks, confirm, move, add or remove splits, re-run silence detection with other settings, name the tracks or paste a tracklist, leave tracks out, mark a recording done, export it, apply the cuts, and download a recording from a link. What Claude changes in the folder open in the window shows up there within a second.

sections.heading: Added
items: Light mode. TrackCut now matches your computer's light or dark setting and follows it when it changes. The sun/moon button at the top right switches between the two. The video frame stays black in both.

sections.heading: Changed
items: Splitter is now called TrackCut. Your Pro licence, settings, downloaded tools and the edits saved in your folders all carry over: a folder's `splitter.cutlist.json` is still read, and becomes `trackcut.cutlist.json` the first time you change something in it. On macOS the update installs as TrackCut.app; once it runs, you can delete Splitter.app from Applications.

sections.heading: Changed
items: TrackCut now uses the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0 and has updated branding. This means the software is free for personal use, but commercial use requires a license. The company name has changed to Mayorana, and the copyright notice has been updated accordingly.

sections.heading: Added
items: TrackCut now shares anonymous usage statistics: whether it is installed and opened, its version and your operating system. It is on by default; a note at the bottom of the window tells you once, and nothing is sent before you have seen it. **Turn off** there stops it for good and deletes anything not yet sent. Your files, data and accounts are never part of it. It also stays off if `DO_NOT_TRACK`, `DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK` or `MAYORANA_NO_TELEMETRY` is set.

sections.heading: Changed
items: Packaging only — no user-visible change.

sections.heading: Added
items: Videos without sound can be cut. They open like any other video, with the picture shown and a flat timeline, and you place every split yourself with **M**, since there is no silence to find. Their clips, and the copy that **Apply cuts** makes, are picture only.
**URL…** with **Video** now downloads videos posted without sound, as is common on X, instead of failing. Asking for **Audio** on such a video now says to pick **Video** instead.

sections.heading: Changed
items: Packaging only — no user-visible change.

sections.heading: Added
items: The version you are running now shows next to the TrackCut name at the top of the sidebar and in the window title, so it is at hand when you report a problem or check whether an update installed.

A **Get Pro…** button at the top of the file list opens the licence window, where you buy TrackCut Pro or paste your key. It reads **Pro ✓** once your licence is active. Clicking **TrackCut** still opens the same window.

sections.heading: Changed
items: Without TrackCut Pro, an export now writes the first 10 tracks of each recording. Splitting, reviewing and naming are not limited: when a recording has more tracks, the export bar says how many and **TrackCut Pro exports all** opens the licence window. A vinyl side, an EP or a short set still fits in the free version; with Pro, every track is exported, as before.

sections.heading: Added
items: TrackCut Pro licences. Click **TrackCut** at the top of the file list to paste the licence key from your purchase email. The key is checked on your computer, with no account and nothing sent anywhere, and a **Pro** badge shows once it is active. **Remove from this computer** frees it for another one.

sections.heading: Fixed
items: The video preview works on Windows web views that refuse to load media from a local address. When that happens the preview falls back to the app's own channel, so the picture still shows instead of an error.

sections.heading: Changed
items: The notes for every release, with its download, are now published at [mayorana.ch/en/apps/trackcut/releases](https://mayorana.ch/en/apps/trackcut/releases).

sections.heading: Added
items: A download log in the sidebar: what yt-dlp printed for the last URL download, kept after it ends. It opens by itself when a download fails, so the reason can be read instead of guessed.

sections.heading: Added
items: Videos: MP4, M4V and MOV files with AAC audio are listed next to the recordings and split on their sound, with the picture shown where a recording shows its overview waveform.

Video export: one MP4 clip per kept track, cut exactly on the splits, with title, album and track number. The clips are re-encoded by ffmpeg, which is fetched on first use (about 30 MB, SHA-256 checked) and never bundled.
**URL…** can download the video instead of only its audio: picture and sound are fetched separately and merged into one MP4.

sections.heading: Added
items: An update banner: the app checks mayorana.ch for a newer version and links straight to the download for the platform it is running on.

sections.heading: Changed
items: First release with a macOS build, signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized.

sections.heading: Added
items: Silence at track edges is cut from the export by default. Detection now tags every quiet stretch, lead-in and tail included; where one touches a track's edge it is trimmed, keeping 0.25 s on each side so quiet attacks and fades survive. **G** keeps a silence or cuts it again. Splits don't move, and the track list shows each track's length after the cut.

sections.heading: Fixed
items: Pressing Enter in the **URL…** dialog no longer crashes the app.

sections.heading: Added
items: First downloadable release. Silence detection suggests the splits, you review each one by ear from the keyboard, then export: MP3 without re-encoding (gapless), or MP3/FLAC/WAV with EBU R128 loudness, ReplayGain tags and optional normalisation. Titles, a batch export queue and A/B listening included.

sections.heading: Changed
items: **URL…** downloads through yt-dlp and Deno instead of ffmpeg. Both are fetched on first use and checked against their published SHA-256 sums, and yt-dlp updates itself at most once a day. The AAC or MP3 stream is fetched directly and AAC is decoded to WAV, so nothing needs installing.

sections.heading: Changed
items: Tagged, but the release build failed and nothing was published. The first downloadable version is 0.1.2.
